title: Effects of water turbidity on the growth and health status of marron (Cherax cainii Austin, 2002)
content:
Abstract

Water turbidity, a key environmental factor in freshwater aquaculture systems, influences light penetration and thus potentially affects the natural productivity of the water, as well as the physiological and behavioral responses of cultured species. This study evaluated the effects of two turbidity levels of freshwater microalgae, Chlorella spp., and a commercial product called blue dye (Aquatic™ Blue) on the health and growth performance of 0+ marron, Cherax cainii, over 120 days. A total of 225 marron were exposed to five treatments: clear water used as a control, low and high algae density, and low and high Aquatic™ Blue dye concentrations. Hematological parameters, including hemocyanin levels and total and differential hemocyte counts, were measured at post 0 h, 24 h, 7 days, 30 days, 60 days, and 120 days. The marron cultured in turbid conditions, regardless of the levels or sources, showed significantly higher growth and hematological responses. Hemocyanin concentrations were high in turbid waters, indicating enhanced immune activity. These findings suggest that controlled turbidity can enhance the growth and health status of marron in aquaculture systems, with potential applications for improving culture practices and animal welfare. Moreover, the use of blue dye could be an alternative method in winter when the natural production of algae is limited.
